rules.statement: In `global.json`, set `sdk.rollForward` to `latestMinor` and `sdk.allowPrerelease` to `false`; don't use `disable` or `latestPatch`.
rules.why: `latestMinor` rolls the build forward to the newest installed SDK of the major, and an older SDK stops `dotnet` at once with the version it needs. `disable` or `latestPatch` locks the build to one band and refuses newer SDKs and servicing releases, which goes against keeping the SDK current.
rules.check: Look at the `sdk` section of any changed `global.json`: `rollForward` other than `latestMinor`, `allowPrerelease: true`, or either setting missing.

rules.statement: Set the `global.json` SDK version to the newest serviced .NET SDK release that is at least three days old, not to the lowest band that happens to compile.
rules.why: Only the newest SDK bands get servicing releases. A floor at an older band lets in SDKs that still have unfixed bugs, such as compiler bugs that break correct code.
rules.check: Check that a changed `global.json` `sdk.version` is the newest released SDK of its major that is past the three-day cooldown, and that the change doesn't lower it to an older band.

rules.statement: Don't raise the `global.json` SDK version above the SDK in the digest-pinned SDK image that the repository's Dockerfiles build from.
rules.why: The image builds read the same `global.json`, so a version above the image's SDK breaks them until the image digest is updated.
rules.check: When `global.json` `sdk.version` changes, compare it with the SDK version of the pinned `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk` image in the Dockerfiles. Flag it if the new version is higher and the same change doesn't update the image digest.

rules.statement: Don't rewrite correct C# to get around a known compiler bug (such as a false `CS8620` on a `params IEnumerable<T>` extension-block member); raise the SDK floor to a release that has the fix.
rules.why: The calls are correct C#. A rewrite that satisfies one compiler bug still leaves the next call that the same bug miscompiles.
rules.check: Look for diffs that reshape correct calls (for example, wrapping a single argument in an array or adding casts or `!`) just to silence a compiler diagnostic that a newer SDK fixes.

rules.statement: Keep a `dotnet-sdk` ecosystem entry in `.github/dependabot.yml` with a three-day cooldown that ignores major-version updates, and don't use CI workflows to pin the SDK separately from `global.json`.
rules.why: Dependabot keeps the SDK floor current without hand edits, and major versions are planned migrations. CI installs the SDK from `global.json` (`actions/setup-dotnet` with `global-json-file`), so a floor change needs no workflow change.
rules.check: Flag a `dependabot.yml` change that removes the `dotnet-sdk` entry, drops its cooldown, or allows major updates. Flag workflows that hard-code a `dotnet-version` instead of using `global-json-file`.
